ref_speedup_note: Anchor 4.0 calibrated in oracle mode on the authoring CPU lane (Intel Sapphire Rapids). tests/ref_speedup.txt is authoritative at scoring; this file is only the in-image fallback. See tests/ref_speedup.caveat.md to re-measure on your hardware.
target_hardware: cpu (x86-64 Sapphire Rapids; pure-Python stdlib, fixed FNV-1a/sha1 hash -> deterministic count, no profiler)
value_axis: recompile_count = number of DISTINCT identities produced by identity_key over a fixed labeled workload of build-specs; the naive baseline emits one identity per spelling (more identities than true classes), a full normalizer emits one per true equivalence class
safety_gate: no false merge: over the whole labeled workload no identity may be shared by two DIFFERENT true equivalence classes (checked by count_bench.py verify and by the no_false_merge_full_workload case); two specs differing only in target profile are DIFFERENT classes, so dropping the target profile from the identity is a false merge = correctness failure -> reward 0
